title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quantization profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: reduce per-token serving cost across hosted and dedicated deployments by shipping conservative, safe defaults and tooling for automated tuning of batching/caching/quantization. This PR implements three coordinated deliverables: 1) Autotune defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching based on observed request size distributions (histogram-based heuristics + conservative SLO guardrails); 2) New quantization profiles (int8/4-bit fallback profiles) surfaced in the model catalog and used by the runtime autoselector; 3) Unit-economics tooling (uecon) to simulate cost/latency tradeoffs and generate suggested config patches for customers and Dedicated pools. Summary of changes: - Add histogram-based traffic analyzer that computes per-route optimal batch window and cache TTL defaults and writes suggestions to /configs/autotune-defaults.yaml - Add runtime hooks to apply suggested batch/window sizes and cache prefixes at route initialization with safe rollback on SLO violations - Add quant profiles: q-int8-fast, q-int8-stable, q-4bit-safe and integrate them into model_selector with compatibility matrix (cpu/gpu, sequence length ranges) - Add uecon CLI and library: uecon estimate --route <id> --profile <profile> to compute expected tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, and projected per-1M-token cost given current infra pricing - Instrumentation: emit autotune.suggested_{batch_size,delay_ms,cache_ttl} and uecon.estimate_{cost_per_1M,latency_p95} metrics to console and metrics pipeline - Tests: unit tests for analyzer heuristics, integration test that runs against perf-canary to validate no SLO regressions on sample traffic - Docs: update redwood-docs/cost-optimization page with examples and migration notes Rollout plan: feature is behind runtime flag: runtime.autotune.enabled=false by default for private deployments; we enable for hosted gradually (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with a canary on low-throughput routes. Backwards compatibility: defaults are suggestions only; existing explicit route config takes precedence. In Dedicated, admin can opt-in via the console. Measured impact on internal perf-canary (gpt-medium family workloads): median per-token cost reduction 18%, p95 latency change < +3% in steady-state; cold-starts unchanged. Checklist: [x] Analyzer algorithm implemented and unit-tested [x] Runtime hooks and rollback implemented [x] Quant profiles added and benchmarked [x] uecon CLI + estimators added [x] Metrics + dashboards updated [x] Docs and release notes updated Related: ENG-4821 (autotune design), ENG-4999 (uecon MVP).
